output:
Actions taken (tools used): I began with a full portfolio snapshot and analytics, checked market details/histories and timers for targeted markets, ran concise news checks for catalysts, ran risk sizing, then placed a trade.

Current portfolio snapshot (from initial calls)
- Cash: $1,023.19
- Invested: $1,207.54
- Estimated bankroll: $2,230.73
- Risk alert: one position (Trump hush-money YES) exceeds 20% of bankroll.

Immediate trade executed
- Trade - Will Trump successfully appeal the hush money case? — Bet 45 MANA on NO
- Reason - High concentration in YES (risk alert). I believe NO is slightly undervalued vs my view (I used a 60% belief for NO vs market 55.9%), and the risk gate recommended a Kelly-style cap ~ $45.7; I sized to $45 (≈2.0% of bankroll, ~4.0% of bankroll exposure reduction relative to that single position). Placed as a market order. Bet ID: ROC5tQp6SAAz.

Why I traded (thesis + evidence)
- Position concentration problem: portfolio_analytics flagged the hush-money YES position as over 20% of bankroll (top position $802). Reducing net exposure was priority.
- Catalyst: recent reporting confirms appeals activity is ongoing but no near-term resolution expected; appeals give Trump opportunities but outcomes are uncertain. AP reported that appeals courts have given him additional opportunities to challenge the conviction (AP summary crawled: “Trump gets another shot at erasing his hush money conviction” — AP News). I used this to form a 60% subjective NO (i.e., he will not successfully appeal) vs the market NO price 55.9% — small edge only; bet sized per risk gate.
  - Source: AP article (web-scraped): https://apnews.com/article/trump-hush-money-appeal-federal-court-conviction-12d2c85c0f90715d64f1764de335df04

Sizing and risk controls
- Risk gate checks: I ran the risk_gate. A large $300 contrarian bet would have failed (exceeded single-run exposure limits). The Kelly-style cap at my assumed edge was ~$45.7. I bet $45 to stay within the cap and not overconcentrate. This is ~2.02% of bankroll (45 / 2,230.73).
- Bankroll preservation: small targeted hedge rather than attempting to fully close the large YES exposure (which the sell tool did not allow me to liquidate in this session — see below).

Sell / hedge decisions for current holdings
- Hush-money market: I attempted to liquidate YES shares directly but the sell call returned "no sellable shares" despite the portfolio showing a large YES position (API inconsistency). Because I could not liquidate the existing YES holding with the sell tool, I hedged by buying NO ( executed above ) to reduce net exposure.
- US strike Iran by end of February (market closes 2026-02-28, ~6 days): I hold both YES and NO in this market in the portfolio (small, mixed exposure). I reviewed recent market history and did quick news checks — no clear, credible, immediate-catalyst indicating a high probability of a US strike this week. Given short time to resolution and mixed existing exposure, I am not adding new size right now; instead I’ll monitor intelligence/press briefings. Evidence: searches show ongoing 2026 US–Iran tensions and repeated reporting, but I found no single imminent-strike confirmation in major outlets during this session (DDG results: general coverage & Wikipedia pages on the 2026 US–Iran crisis; no breaking confirmation of imminent attack).
  - Source examples: DDG results for “February 2026 US strike Iran latest news” (no definitive imminent-strike story surfaced in the quick check).

Other markets scanned (opportunities & research)
- US — Iran nuclear deal by end of June? (closes 2026-06-30, YES ~30.8%): recent bets show some movement toward YES; I have a small YES position already. There are diplomatic negotiation catalysts through spring; this is a longer-dated political/diplomatic play. I am not adding size now but will watch signs of confident negotiation breakthroughs (e.g., official statements, minister-level meetings, leaked drafts). Recent market volume and bets show institutional interest.
  - Source: manifold market history checked in-session.
- Aaron Rodgers retirement (multichoice): interesting long-dated sports market but not compelling edge for me today.

Planned follow-up research (concrete items)
1. Hush-money appeals docket & calendar: track court filings, appellate argument schedule, and any stay orders. Immediate next research: check New York appellate court filings and local press (NYT / AP) for scheduled oral argument or decisions. If a near-term ruling date appears that materially increases chance of a successful appeal, reassess.
2. Iran strike intel: monitor Pentagon/POTUS/State Dept briefings and top-tier outlets (AP, NYT, Reuters) for confirmed US strike orders or credible leaks. If a confirmed strike threat surfaces, plan to scale into YES on the “strike by end of Feb” market—else stay neutral.
3. For larger, lower-frequency risks (e.g., “US-Iran nuclear deal by June”), gather diplomatic meeting schedules (EU/UN/Iran delegates) and trustable reporting on negotiation progress; place small limit orders only when my edge widens.

Why no additional trades now
- Concentration: the portfolio currently has large exposures; priority is hedging/reducing concentration rather than adding new speculative positions.
- Market-specific reasons: the “strike Iran by end of Feb” market has little actionable new publicly-available intel in this session; adding size into a closing market with mixed current exposure is riskier than waiting for clearer information.

Cash after trade
- Cash before trade: $1,023.19
- Trade executed: -$45
- Estimated cash remaining (post-trade): $978.19
- Estimated bankroll unchanged aside from repositioning: ~$2,230 (portfolio invested increased by $45).

Final summary
1) Summary - Reduced net exposure to a single concentrated political position (Trump hush-money YES) by placing a small, risk-gated hedge: 45 MANA on NO in the relevant market. I scanned nearby short-dated geopolitical markets and found nothing that justified adding new risk this run; I will monitor and follow the concrete research items listed above.
Trade - Will Trump successfully appeal the hush money case? — Bet 45 MANA on NO
Reason - Hedge to reduce concentration (risk_gate recommended cap ~$45.7 based on my 60% NO belief vs market ~55.9%); AP reporting shows appeals process ongoing but uncertain; selling the large YES holding via the API failed in-session so I hedged instead.

Remaining cash / pending research
- Remaining cash (approx): $978.19
- Pending research: appeals docket timing (hush money), credible intel on any imminent US strike on Iran, diplomatic progress toward a US-Iran deal by June.

If you want, I can:
- Try to liquidate the large hush-money YES position again (sell attempt failed in this run) — I can retry a sell command now, or
- Place small, conditional limit orders on the Iran strike or nuclear deal markets if you want active exposure, or
- Begin the deeper/continuous monitoring jobs for appeals docket + foreign-policy briefings and place limit trades automatically when predefined triggers occur. Which would you prefer?
